title: "Teaching Guide"

## How a lecture is built

This guide describes the Volume I decks. The Volume II decks are being rebuilt to the same standard.

Each deck is one lecture, on one chapter of the book or on one part of a larger chapter. A lecture opens with a real system, failure, or number, works through the chapter's core ideas in four to six sections, and closes by returning to the opening example. Each section opens with a divider slide that names its question and the chapter sections to read. A progress line in the header shows where the lecture is.

Most slides carry one idea and one picture. Figures build one step at a time, so the class looks at one thing while it is explained. Every number on a slide has its source in small type at the bottom of the slide.

Use the slides as the classroom layer of the curriculum: assign the [textbook](https://mlsysbook.ai) chapter for reading, use [TinyTorch](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/) for implementation, the [Hardware Kits](https://mlsysbook.ai/kits/) for deployment, and the [Instructor Hub](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/) for syllabi, assessment, and TA workflows.

### Speaker notes

Every slide has notes written as instructions to the instructor. Each note gives:

- whether the slide is `[CORE]` or `[OPTIONAL]`;
- what to say at each step of a build;
- **ENGAGE**: a question for the class, with the expected answer and what a wrong answer reveals;
- **WARN**: a common misconception and how to address it;
- **LINK**: where the idea comes from or returns in another lecture.

The optional slides can be skipped for a shorter class without breaking the argument.

In PowerPoint or Keynote, the notes appear in the notes pane and in presenter view. With the PDF, the notes are in the source as `\note{...}` on each slide, and `make notes` builds a PDF that shows each slide beside its notes.

### Activities

Activities recur throughout each lecture, and each is marked by a tag in the slide's top corner:

- **Predict**: students commit to an answer before the slide reveals it.
- **Estimate**: a short calculation from given numbers, worked on the next step.
- **Diagnose**: students name the cause of a failure or the resource that limits a system.
- **Discuss**: a question for pairs, with no single answer.
- **Vote**: true or false, or a choice among options, by show of hands.
- **Retrieval** or **Recall**: students recall an earlier idea with their notes closed.

## Semester plan

Volume I is planned for a 14-week semester with two lectures a week. Lecture 0 introduces the course, and each chapter has one lecture. The larger chapters have a second lecture that teaches what the first leaves to the reading. The [Volume I page](vol1.qmd) lists the decks in teaching order.

## Changing the slides

The slides are LaTeX Beamer source, open for any change.

```
slides/
  assets/beamerthememlsys.sty   # the theme: colors, header, footer, macros
  assets/kit/                   # figures shared across a volume (the stack, one node)
  vol1/<deck>/
    <deck>.tex                  # the slides and their notes
    images/make_figs.py         # draws every plot in the deck
    images/                     # figures, photos, and SOURCES.yml (photo credits)
  Makefile
```

### Building a deck

```bash
cd slides
make build-01_introduction            # the presenting PDF
make handout V=1 D=01_introduction    # one page per slide, final state of each build
make notes V=1 D=01_introduction      # each slide beside its speaker notes
make pptx-vol1                        # PowerPoint for every Volume I deck
```

Output goes to `_build/vol1/`. A build needs a TeX distribution with `pdflatex` and the Metropolis Beamer theme, plus Inkscape to convert figures. PowerPoint conversion also needs poppler and the Python packages `python-pptx` and `Pillow`. Build a deck's notes before converting it, so the speaker notes are copied into the PowerPoint file.

### Editing

1. Fork the [repository](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book).
2. Edit `<deck>.tex`, or change a plot in `images/make_figs.py` and run it.
3. Rebuild the deck and look at every page you changed.

Figures are SVG files, converted to PDF by the build. Edit them in any vector editor.

### The theme

`assets/beamerthememlsys.sty` sets the look of every deck. Each volume has its own accent color, chosen in the deck's `\mlsyssetup{volume=...}` line, so all of a volume's decks change together when the theme changes.
